Thanks for the quick onboarding call this morning. Legal and our broker had a couple of follow-ups on the insurance requirements in the draft order form before we route to carrier. Can you confirm the following so we can get final pricing from Aon:

4) Signatory constraints: our procurement team needs to know if there are any signatory broker constraints (carrier countersignatures, power-of-attorney on endorsement), or if we can upload to DocuSign and you accept broker-delivered endorsements after countersign.

We attached our sample COI for reference. Happy to hop on a 15m call with your insurance/ops if helpful.

Hi Maya — thanks, and great questions. Looping in Olga (insurance ops) and David (legal) to confirm details below. High-level answers:

- We generally accept claims-made for cyber with a retroactive date at or prior to service start.
- E&O (Professional Liability) is typically $2M×2M (per occurrence/aggregate).
- Temporary COI is OK to proceed at signature provided the carrier agrees to issue the required endorsement within 30 days; we can accept 30-day bridge in most cases.
- For Additional Insured, we need the endorsement that names: "Redwood Inference, its subsidiaries and affiliates, and their officers, directors and employees" — Olga will drop the template and confirm whether Contractual Liability must be included.

Olga / David — can you confirm the endorsement id (insurer form or CG language) we prefer to see for this type of SOW, and whether the AI should be limited to GL or extended to Professional Liability for services with data processing? Also confirm signatory expectations (carrier POA acceptable?).

Hannah

Hi all — quick insurance ops note and the endorsement template attached. Summary for Stratus:

1) Limits & basis
- Commercial General Liability (CGL): 1M per occ / 2M agg (standard).
- Professional Liability / Errors & Omissions (E&O): 2M per claim / 2M aggregate (claims-made is acceptable for E&O if retro date covers inception).
- Cyber (Privacy/Network Security): 5M aggregate, claims-made is industry standard; require retroactive date no later than service start on order form. If Stratus insists on occurrence, we can escalate but expect pricing impact.
- Excess/umbrella: 5M recommended where primary limits are low.

2) Additional Insured (AI) & endorsement text
- We require an AI endorsement that names: "Redwood Inference, its subsidiaries and affiliates, and their officers, directors, employees and agents."
- For most SaaS/hosting relationships, AI on CGL is required; we do not usually require AI on E&O/professional liability unless there are on-prem/third-party integration obligations that create vicarious exposure. If Stratus' work includes configuring or customizing code that accesses Redwood customer data, legal may request AI on E&O — flagging to David.
- Preferred endorsement: carrier-supplied endorsement (CG 20 10/20 37 equivalent) or a policy endorsement naming Redwood; worksheet attached: redwood_addl_insured_template.pdf

3) Timing and temporary COI
- Temporary COI acceptable at signature. Endorsement to follow within 30 calendar days. If carrier cannot commit, we can accept a 14-day bridge in a few strategic deals but 30 is standard.

4) Signatory / carrier process
- Carrier POA is acceptable for endorsements so long as the broker confirms authority. DocuSign upload + broker delivery after countersign is a common flow; please include the broker contact for tracking (Lisa at Aon is copied).

Attachments: redwood_addl_insured_template.pdf (pdf) — redactable endorsement language; MSA_insurance_redlines_20260802.docx (docx) — my proposed redline to the order form's insurance section showing optional AI-on-E&O checkbox.

Olga Petrov
Insurance Operations Manager
Redwood Inference

Thanks — a couple legal clarifications for the thread:

- Additional insured: we should limit AI on Professional Liability to explicit integration/configuration work where Stratus' negligence could directly create loss to Redwood customers. Blanket AI on E&O increases carrier pushback. Proposed language in the redline: "Addl Insured on CGL; AI on Professional Liability only if the Scope of Work includes customer-specific configuration, deployment, or agent-based access to Redwood customer data."

- Cyber claims-made: acceptable with retro date <= start. We should require 30-day notice for changes to retro date and a carrier attestation if retro date is materially later than inception.

- Temporary COI: legal is comfortable with a 30-day endorsement delivery window; if we see longer than 30 days, require interim escrow of funds or a holdback (rare).

If Stratus is flexible on AI-on-E&O language, we can move forward without escalation to underwriting. Otherwise, we will need a short call with their broker and possibly an underwriter exception.

David Kim
Senior Counsel, Contracts
